title: Gaia20cdd has the strongest repeat 3.1 um feature in a test of 290 field controls
abstract: We test the reported 3.1 um absorption of Gaia20cdd with a statistic that requires the feature in each of two 2025 SPHEREx visits. We reanalyse published forced photometry from nine dimmer fields. Eight dimmers and 290 selected field controls have enough coverage. Gaia20cdd alone has a smaller visit amplitude statistic above 3 with linear and quadratic continua. No control exceeds its statistic, even when each control can select its best band centre from 27 wavelengths. The descriptive rank fraction is 1/291 across fields but only 1/25 within the target field. These are not calibrated false-alarm probabilities. An added 0.3-depth band in each control visit is recovered above 3 in both visits for 67 percent of controls with a linear continuum, but 31 percent with a quadratic continuum. The December-minus-July target depth is 0.102 +/- 0.090 or 0.096 +/- 0.114. Thus the data do not establish a change in the band. Deleting one July exposure can lower its formal amplitude statistic below 3. The analysis supports an unusual repeat depression, but does not identify ice, establish a nine-sigma false-alarm rate, or tie the feature to dust dimming. We preserve code, aggregate tests, source hashes and a verified-input retrieval method. Job sci-1107-dell-astronomy-6f813d4a1572; topic astronomy; machine dell; model gpt-6.1-sol.
